changes: Dataset created. No profiles have been researched yet. Institutions on an official list are rated High from those lists alone (rubric 1.1), with each listing shown as evidence; institutions on no list are not rated.

Pilot research: the seven Seven Sons of National Defence universities (Beihang, BIT, HIT, HEU, NWPU, NUAA, NJUST) researched and verified with sourced, archived evidence, including documented US export-control and espionage cases; each is rated Very high.

Second research batch: ten PLA bodies on Canada’s NRO list (the Academy of Military Science and its Academy of Military Medical Sciences, and eight PLA Air Force schools) researched and verified with sourced, archived evidence; each is rated Very high.

Third research batch: ten more PLA bodies on Canada’s NRO list (the Air Force Research Institute, the Xi’an flight academy and eight PLA Army schools, including Army Medical University with its hospitals marked for batch-check matching) researched and verified; each is rated Very high.

Fourth research batch: three PLA schools, four bodies Canada and the US list as part of China’s nuclear-weapons complex (CAEP), a CETC research academy listed by the US over surveillance in Xinjiang, and two listed universities (BESTI, BUPT) researched and verified; eight are rated Very high and two High.

Fifth research batch: CAEP itself and China Jiuyuan Trading Corporation, which Canada and the US list as part of it; the PLA’s aerodynamics research centre (CARDC); Dalian Naval Academy; two People’s Armed Police academies (the Coast Guard Academy and PAP Engineering University); two universities run by the Ministry of Public Security (CPPU, CIPUC); and two listed Chinese Academy of Sciences institutes (Shenyang Institute of Automation, Institute of Computing Technology) researched and verified; eight are rated Very high and two High. HPSTAR’s Chinese name moved from CAEP’s record to its own.

The US Section 1286 list (FY2025 edition, published 23 July 2026) and Japan's End User List (revision of 29 September 2025) are now loaded, so no list reads "Not checked yet". 37 institutions are new to the tracker, 14 that were on no other list are now rated High from the 1286 list, and three institutions the US lists named twice are now one record each.

The official lists name academies and institutes of CASC, CASIC and AVIC, not the groups themselves, so each listed unit now has its own record and the groups no longer show as listed (they are not rated until researched); a group's profile names its listed units. Institutions already in the tracker that a list names under a company-style name, such as CAEP's trading companies, now show that list. 11 institutions are new to the tracker, and two that had duplicate records (NIIPKh in Sergiev Posad, FNPC Start) are now one record each.

Sixth research batch: three PLA schools (Information Engineering University, the Army Institute of NBC Defence and the Army Command College in Nanjing), the PAP Logistics University, a national defence key laboratory at NUDT that the US lists (Key Laboratory of Information Systems Engineering), Jiangnan Social University, which Chinese government notices place under the Ministry of State Security, the Ministry of Public Security’s Institute of Forensic Science, USTC’s Hefei national research centre for physical sciences at the microscale, Hunan University and the Nanjing Institute of Information Technology researched and verified; seven are rated Very high and three High.

Seventh research batch: ten PLA bodies on Canada’s NRO list researched and verified: the National Defense University, the National University of Defense Technology and eight PLA Navy schools and research bodies (the Naval Command College, Naval University of Engineering, Naval Aviation University, Naval Medical University with its three hospitals marked for batch-check matching, Navy Submarine Academy, Naval Service Academy, Naval NCO School and Naval Research Academy); each is rated Very high. Five map points were moved to the institutions’ campuses.

Eighth research batch: three People’s Armed Police academies (the Officers College in Chengdu, the Command College in Tianjin and the NCO School in Hangzhou), the PLA Rocket Force Command College, the PLA’s Northwest Institute of Nuclear Technology, CAEP’s Peac Institute of Multiscale Science, two universities run by the Ministry of Public Security (the People’s Public Security University of China and the Railway Police College, renamed Zhengzhou Police College in 2023), the North University of China and the North China Institute of Aerospace Engineering researched and verified; nine are rated Very high and one High. Three map points were moved to the institutions’ campuses or listed addresses.

Ninth research batch: three PLA Rocket Force bodies (its Research Academy, NCO School and University of Engineering), four companies and two institutes that Canada and the US list as part of China’s nuclear-weapons complex (CAEP), and Sichuan University researched and verified; nine are rated Very high and one High. Several map points were moved to the addresses their sources give.

Tenth research batch: ten more institutes that Canada and the US list among the known aliases of China’s nuclear-weapons complex (CAEP) researched and verified: the Southwest Institutes of Chemical Materials, Electronic Engineering, Environmental Testing, Explosives and Chemical Engineering, Fluid Physics (which hosts CAEP’s shock wave and detonation physics key laboratory), General Designing and Assembly, Machining Technology, Materials, Nuclear Physics and Chemistry, and Research and Applications of Special Materials; each is rated Very high.

Eleventh research batch: three more bodies that Canada and the US list as part of China’s nuclear-weapons complex (CAEP: the Southwest Institute of Structural Mechanics, the High Power Laser Laboratory in Shanghai and the Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics), two PLA universities (Space Engineering University, now under the Aerospace Force, and the Army Service Arms University, formed in 2025 from two Army academies), the University of International Relations, which a Chinese provincial notice places under the Ministry of State Security, Tianjin University, the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Xi’an Technological University and the Shenzhen University branch of a national defence key laboratory for automatic target recognition researched and verified; seven are rated Very high and three High.
Common short Chinese names, such as 国防科技大学 for the National University of Defense Technology and 第三军医大学 for Army Medical University, added to six profiles so that the batch check finds them.

Twelfth research batch: ten bodies on the US Section 1286 list researched and verified: Tsinghua University’s Center for International Security and Strategy; Changchun University of Science and Technology, Chongqing University, Chongqing University of Technology and Dalian University of Technology; and five national defence key laboratories hosted by Chinese universities (antennas and microwave technology at Xidian University, electronic measurement technology at North University of China, high-power semiconductor lasers at Changchun University of Science and Technology, lightweight high-strength structural materials at Central South University, and multi-spectral information processing at Huazhong University of Science and Technology), each now named on its host university’s profile; one is rated Very high and nine High.

The Entity List's seven national supercomputing centres (Changsha, Guangzhou, Jinan, Shenzhen, Tianjin, Wuxi and Zhengzhou) are now in the tracker, rated High from that list; their names carry no research word, so the list filter had left them out. CAEP's 15 research institutes now show the Entity List and Japan's End User List, which name them as aliases in CAEP's own entry; both lists had read "Not listed" for them.

Thirteenth research batch: ten bodies on the US Section 1286 list researched and verified: the Joint Logistics Support Force Engineering University, which the PLA formed in 2025 from two Army academies; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Xidian University’s national defence key laboratory for radar signal processing, now named on the university’s profile; and Fudan University, Guilin University of Electronic Technology (until now listed here as Guilin University of Electronic Science and Technology), Hangzhou Dianzi University, Ocean University of China, Shandong University, Shenyang Aerospace University and Shenyang Ligong University; two are rated Very high and eight High.

Fourteenth research batch: five state-owned defence-industry groups that SASTIND lists as such (AECC, AVIC, CASC, CASIC and CEC), which no checked list names, are now rated Very high on that basis; the academy and institute names that MISP had given CASC and CASIC as aliases are removed, since the lists name those units in their own right, and six AECC research institutes are marked for batch-check matching. Also researched and verified: Xinjiang Police College, which the US Commerce Department describes as part of Xinjiang’s public security bureau and links to human rights abuses; Xidian University, with its two national defence key laboratories; and Sun Yat-sen University, the University of Science and Technology of China and Xi’an Jiaotong University. Seven are rated Very high and three High.

Fifteenth research batch: the defence-industry groups CETC, CNNC, NORINCO and China State Shipbuilding Corporation, which SASTIND lists, and China South Industries Group, which calls itself a core force of the defence industry, are rated Very high; so is China Shipbuilding Industry Corporation, which merged into China State Shipbuilding Corporation in 2019 and keeps its record so that co-author lines naming it still match, and the People’s Armed Police Special Police Academy. Beijing University of Chemical Technology and Anhui University, both co-built by SASTIND, are rated High, and COMAC, whose founding shareholders include AVIC and which co-founded AECC, Medium. Former Chinese company names (…集团公司) were added to eight group profiles so that older co-author lines match. Seven are rated Very high, two High and one Medium.

Sixteenth research batch: twelve universities from the rest of the MISP list, none on a checked list and each rated on its own evidence: Central South University, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), China University of Mining and Technology, Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Dalian Minzu University, Donghua University, East China University of Technology, Fuzhou University, Hebei University, Hebei University of Science and Technology, Hefei University of Technology and Heilongjiang Institute of Technology. Rated: 8 High, 3 Medium, 1 Low; Hebei University was verified after the batch, once its sources were checked.

Seventeenth research batch: fifteen universities from the rest of the MISP list, none on a checked list and each rated on its own evidence: Heilongjiang University, Hunan University of Science and Technology, Jiangsu University of Science and Technology, Kunming University of Science and Technology, Lanzhou University of Technology, Nanchang Hangkong University, Southeast University, Zhejiang University, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Jilin University, Peking University, Tsinghua University and Lanzhou University. Rated: 15 High.

Eighteenth research batch: fourteen universities from the rest of the MISP list, none on a checked list and each rated on its own evidence: North China University of Science and Technology, Shandong University of Technology, Shanghai University, Shenzhen University, Soochow University, South China University of Technology, Southwest University of Science and Technology, Tiangong University, the University of Science and Technology Beijing, the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, the University of South China, Xiamen University, Xiangtan University and Yanshan University. Rated: 14 High.

Nineteenth research batch: three more universities from the rest of the MISP list, Nanjing University (secrecy qualification), Henan University of Science and Technology (SASTIND co-construction and defence-specialty disciplines) and Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications (military-industry projects). Rated: 2 High, 1 Medium.

Twentieth research batch: the eleven research institutes of the Academy of Military Medical Sciences that the US Entity List and the Section 1286 list name, each a unit of the PLA’s Academy of Military Science, now have records of their own linked to the academy. Rated: 11 Very high.

Twenty-first research batch: eighteen research institutes of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC) that the US Entity List names now have records of their own, linked to CETC, with the reason each was listed; three of them (CETC 13, 29 and 55) were listed for the illicit procurement of US technology for military end use. Rated: 18 Very high.

Twenty-second research batch: 25 research institutes and academies of China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC), the naval shipbuilding group, which the US Entity List names, now have records of their own, linked to CSSC, with their Chinese names before and after the 2019 merger and the reason each was listed. Rated: 25 Very high.

Twenty-third research batch: 29 academies and research institutes of the space and missile groups CASC and CASIC that the US Entity List, the US Military End-User List or Japan’s End User List name now have records of their own, linked to their academies and groups; CASC’s own site lists its eight research academies. Rated: 29 Very high.

Twenty-fourth research batch: 11 listed research institutes of the aviation groups AVIC and AECC and of CETC now have records of their own, linked to their groups, among them AVIC’s 612 Institute (the China Airborne Missile Academy), its Chengdu aircraft design institute and AECC’s Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials. Beijing Aeronautical Manufacturing Technology Research Institute (AVIC’s Institute 625) also carries the 2014 finding that it supplied Iran’s ballistic missile programme. Rated: 11 Very high.

Twenty-fifth research batch: three more listed units now have records of their own: the Wuxi Jiangnan Institute of Computing Technology, which the US Commerce Department says the PLA’s 56th Research Institute owns; the Laboratory of Toxicant Analysis of the Academy of Military Medical Sciences’ Institute of Pharmacology and Toxicology (an OPCW-designated laboratory); and CETC 14’s Nanjing Institute of Radio Technology. Rated: 3 Very high.

Twenty-sixth research batch: four more listed bodies now have records of their own: the CAS Shanghai Institute of Microsystem and Information Technology, which CASI says hosts a defence key laboratory of ambiguous status, and the national supercomputing centres in Changsha, Guangzhou (at Sun Yat-sen University) and Tianjin, listed in 2015 with the PLA’s National University of Defense Technology over the Tianhe supercomputers it built for them. Rated: 4 High.

Twenty-seventh research batch: two research institutes listed with China General Nuclear Power Group in 2019, China Nuclear Power Technology Research Institute and Suzhou Nuclear Power Research Institute, now carry the US finding that they took part in efforts to acquire US nuclear technology and material for diversion to military uses; they stay High on the list. Rated: 2 High.

Rubric 1.2: the armed-forces signals (renamed from “pla” and “pla-collaboration” to “armed-forces” and “armed-forces-collaboration”) and the defence-group signal now cover the armed forces and state defence industries of Russia and Iran as well as China, and the security-agency and nuclear-weapons signals name Russian and Iranian examples. The profiles researched before it now use the new ids; no rating changed.

Twenty-eighth research batch, the first from group 6 under rubric 1.2: 10 Russian Ministry of Defence bodies, among them the 27th Scientific Center, the 33rd Institute and the 48th Institute (which the US government ties to Russia’s chemical and biological weapons programs), the Air and Space Forces’ central research institute and the Main Directorate of Deep Sea Research, are rated Very high as part of the armed forces, and the FSB Criminalistics Institute as part of a security service. OFAC’s separate entry for the 46th Institute now belongs to the Canadian-listed record. Rated: 11 Very high.
